subject: sociology
title: Four Feminisms
welcome_lead: From Friedan's polite reforms to Greer's radical revolts, meet the four strands of feminism every GCSE answer needs.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology adventure on liberal, radical, Marxist and Black feminism.
final_note: Name the strand, name a thinker, name an example — three steps to AO2.

concepts.def: A society organised so men hold most power.
Reform: equal rights via laws and education.
Patriarchy is the root cause; sweep it away.
Race, class and gender combine in oppression.

walkthroughs.body_html: Betty Friedan's The Feminine Mystique (1963) sparked liberal feminism. The aim is equal rights through laws like the Equal Pay Act 1970 and Sex Discrimination Act 1975. Progress matters; gradual change works.
Germaine Greer's The Female Eunuch (1970) and Susan Brownmiller's work argue patriarchy runs deeper than law. Family, sexuality and culture all need transforming, not just tweaking.

Marxist feminist Heidi Hartmann argues capitalism uses women's unpaid housework. bell hooks and Kimberlé Crenshaw insist white feminism missed how race and class layer onto gender — this is intersectionality.
